transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 10:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Host: Aditi Rao
Attendees: Aditi, Samir, Elena, Marcus, Priya, Jonah, Leah, Claire

Summary (auto): Leadership gave a quick update on runway, reliability, hiring, and product priorities. Open Q&A at the end.

[00:00] Aditi: Hey everyone, good morning, thanks for joining. We promised a tight agenda — two big things: quick finance/risk, then product/ops priorities. We'll leave 10 minutes for questions, try to keep mics muted otherwise.

[00:28] Samir: Quick add — engineering is going to call out a postmortem summary on the January outage, and a plan. Small correction, that was actually the late-Feb event but yeah.

[01:02] Elena: Thanks. I want to start with product priorities, we've been hearing from customers about dedicated throughput and also friction in private onboarding, so Q2 focus is: 1) Dedicated capacity expansion and better autoscale profiles, 2) Private onboarding checklist + console flows, 3) Console UX for rollouts and tracing.

[01:40] Marcus: On the infra side, we are leaning towards a mix of reserved pools with burstable shared nodes. The goal is to keep p95 under 120ms for our 8k token workloads while lowering cost per token by ~12%. We'll need the product to pin the sequence and common-path configs so kernel selection can be optimized.

[02:10] Priya: Ops note: the runbook in prod still has gaps around KMS rotation and the audit logs. We saw multiple handoffs during the most recent incident. We'll do a chair drill to exercise that later this month.

[02:45] Aditi: Ok let's call that the reliability bucket. Jonah, short finance update?

[02:52] Jonah: Sure — runway's healthy but not infinite. Base plan assumes 18 months at current burn, hiring adds pressure. We model three scenarios if we accelerate Dedicated sales: conservative, mid, aggressive. We'll update the sheet and share by Thursday.

[03:18] Leah: Hiring — people ops is prioritizing 8 IC hires across infra and product, plus two senior SRE roles. We are pushing for diversity slates, and expedite interviews for top candidates.

[03:36] Audience: (muted hand raise) Question: any changes to compensation/hiring bands?

[03:40] Aditi: Not today, we'll share updated bands in People drop. Focus on leveling and remote allowances.

[04:05] Claire (Partner lead): Quick 30s from partner side — a few customers in EMEA asked for on-prem/offline options — the Private package + HSM/KMS needs clearer docs for SOC 2 auditors; we can push joint materials.

[04:40] Elena: Good call. We'll mark security docs as priority in the private onboarding epic. Note: some of our internal names are getting garbled in transcripts — I keep seeing 'Redwood Privet' in the notes — that's the transcription, not a new product.

[05:10] Samir: Back to the outage postmortem: root cause was a cascading KV cache invalidation from a partially deployed model variant, combined with a bad autoscale threshold. Result: degraded latencies across a small fraction of customers. We patched the threshold and rolled back the model rollout.

[05:44] Marcus: Follow-ups: 1) stricter canary gating in Console, 2) autoscale policy sanity checks in Dedicated pools, 3) KV cache health checks and metrics in the runtime. We'll instrument a db of known-safe model variants to avoid the cascade.

[06:20] Priya: Ops will run a tabletop on 3/27 to simulate the handoffs — engineering, support, and CS must attend. We'll run a 90-minute session.

[06:45] Aditi: Ok, moving to product priorities. Elena?

[06:50] Elena: We'll trade off Dedicated throughput vs. Private onboarding polish. For rapid revenue, expand Dedicated pools, but for enterprise deals we must close Private onboarding friction — docs, SSO/SAML sanity, audit log exports. My ask: rank these bets by revenue impact and effort.

[07:20] Samir: Engineering says Dedicated expansion is less risky short-term, but Private has higher ACV for target customers. There's also a comp between doing aggressive quantization work vs. UX.

[07:42] Marcus: Note on quantization: some of our kernel paths are fragile across model families; big gains possible but with regression risk. We need a guardrail: per-model regression tests and a rollback plan.

[08:10] Aditi: Let's capture the experiment plan — Elena to own the one-pager.

[08:18] Elena: Will do. Also planning a small internal beta for new Console tracing hooks — SEs will test.

[08:35] Audience (Speaker 1): Slight cross talk, uh is there a timeline for the Dedicated marketing push?

[08:40] Leah: Growth will coordinate once the capacity plan is solid — aiming mid-April for campaign kickoff.

[09:05] Jonah: On the budget, I want to highlight that a 10% increase in Dedicated revenue can materially extend runway; the team needs a clear sales playbook for Dedicated upsells.

[09:34] Marcus: SEs — we'll make a playbook template: sizing, latency/cost targets, and a benchmark sheet customers can run. That should help sales close faster.

[10:02] Aditi: Ok we'll make a cross-team task force: Product, Eng, SE, Growth. Elena and Marcus co-own.

[10:15] Claire: On compliance — we should standardize an audit packet for Private customers: SOC 2 summary, KMS integrations, data residency notes. Partners can help bundle.

[10:36] Priya: We'll add audit packet to the Private checklist.

[11:00] (skipping forward)
[11:15] Participant comment: question about Dedicated SLOs — are we changing p99 targets for different tiers?

[11:22] Marcus: Tiering yes — premium customers have stricter p99 and different latency windows. We'll codify in SLAs and in Console UI.

[11:45] Samir: Also FYI the runtime team is finishing a continuous batching improvement that will yield better throughput for long-sequence workloads — this is relevant to Dedicated customers. We'll stage deploy in canary after extra perf testing.

[12:12] Aditi: Quick people update. Leah?

[12:18] Leah: We are hiring 8 ICs and 2 Sr SREs. Interviews are lined up; referral program still open. Also rolling out a discrete manager training for low-core managers in April.

[12:45] Jonah: Financial ask — we will propose flexible hiring scenarios and bring a recommendation next Tuesday.

[13:00] Audience: question about partner GTM timing in EMEA?

[13:05] Claire: Partners ready to pilot co-sell in May, but need Private docs and a demo checklist.

[13:30] Elena: We'll provide a demo kit for partners — pre-baked scripts, benchmark sheet, and a security FAQ.

[14:00] Aditi: Ok let's round this out. Quick wins and risks?

[14:08] Marcus: Quick win: shared benchmark sheet for SEs can cut sales cycle. Risk: kernel regressions when we fast-track quantization without sufficient eval coverage.

[14:28] Priya: Risk: handoff gaps on KMS rotation; if not fixed, could increase compliance time for customers.

[14:42] Aditi: Closing thoughts: focus on Dedicated expansion short term to buy time while we improve Private onboarding for mid-term enterprise deals. We'll reconvene for a tactical check next week.

[15:00] Q&A section (open mic)
[15:05] Speaker 2: Is the Console rollout going to include a way to see per-route token cost estimates?

[15:12] Elena: Yes, that's in the design — token-level cost + latency breakdown per route is in the backlog.

[15:33] Speaker 3: Any change to retention policies for logs?

[15:38] Priya: Not changing retention across the board; we will add per-account retention options for Private customers.

[16:00] (wrap up)

[16:10] Aditi: Thanks everyone. Recap: Elena publishes one-pager by 3/18, Jonah updates forecast by 3/19, Marcus drafts capacity plan by 3/21, Priya runs tabletop on 3/27. SEs and Growth coordinate on Dedicated playbook for mid-April launch.

[16:40] Samir: Thanks — action owners please put items in JIRA and tag me.

[16:55] Meeting end: 10:52 PT

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and transcription artifacts common to Fireflies exports. References to internal product names: Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize. Some words may be garbled (e.g., "Redwood Privet", "KV cash") but intent preserved.
